title: Create a thread by extending the Thread class
question: Create a thread that prints numbers from 1 to 5.
explanation: Override run() with the task and call start() to execute it on a new thread. Calling run() directly would execute on the current thread.

title: Create a thread using Runnable
question: Print a message from a task implemented with Runnable.
explanation: Runnable separates the task from the Thread object and is usually more flexible than subclassing Thread.

title: Create a thread using a lambda expression
question: Use a lambda to run a task on a new thread.
explanation: Runnable is a functional interface, so a lambda can provide its run() implementation.

title: Run two tasks concurrently
question: Start two independent tasks and wait for both to finish.
explanation: Starting both threads before joining allows overlap. join() makes the main thread wait for each worker to finish.

title: Print odd and even numbers using two threads
question: Use two threads to print 1 through 10 in order, with one printing odds and the other evens.
explanation: wait() releases the monitor; notifyAll() wakes the other thread. Conditions are checked in while loops to handle spurious wakeups.

title: Implement a thread-safe counter with synchronized
question: Implement increment and read operations that are safe when called by multiple threads.
explanation: synchronized makes increment atomic with respect to other synchronized calls on the same object and establishes visibility.

title: Implement a counter using AtomicInteger
question: Use AtomicInteger to count increments from multiple threads.
explanation: AtomicInteger uses atomic compare-and-set operations for updates without requiring an explicit synchronized block.

title: Use a ReentrantLock to protect shared state
question: Protect a counter with ReentrantLock and always release the lock.
explanation: The finally block ensures unlock() runs even if an exception occurs. ReentrantLock also supports timed and interruptible acquisition.

title: Demonstrate a volatile flag for thread communication
question: Let one thread stop a worker by updating a shared flag.
explanation: volatile makes writes visible to other threads, but it does not make compound operations such as count++ atomic.

title: Wait for a thread with join()
question: Make the main thread wait for a worker to complete.
explanation: join() blocks the calling thread until the target thread terminates. Handle interruption rather than swallowing it.

title: Interrupt a sleeping thread gracefully
question: Interrupt a worker that is sleeping and handle the interruption correctly.
explanation: InterruptedException clears the interrupt status when thrown; restoring it preserves the signal for callers that need to observe it.

title: Create a daemon thread
question: Create a daemon background thread and start it.
explanation: The JVM can exit when only daemon threads remain. Daemon threads should not be used for work that must finish or save important data.

title: Use ExecutorService to run a task
question: Submit a Runnable to a fixed thread pool and shut down the executor.
explanation: Executors manage worker threads and task queues. Shut them down to avoid leaving non-daemon worker threads running.
complexity: Depends on task queue and pool size

title: Collect a task result using Callable and Future
question: Submit a Callable that returns a value and retrieve the result through Future.
explanation: Callable returns a result and can throw checked exceptions. Future.get() waits for completion and can throw ExecutionException or InterruptedException.

title: Run multiple tasks and collect results with invokeAll
question: Submit multiple Callable tasks and print their results in input order.
explanation: invokeAll waits for all tasks to finish (or be cancelled on interruption) and returns Futures in the same order as the input tasks.

title: Get the first successful result with ExecutorCompletionService
question: Process task results in completion order rather than submission order.
explanation: take() retrieves the next completed task's Future. This is useful when results should be handled as soon as they finish.

title: Use ScheduledExecutorService for repeated work
question: Schedule a task to run every second and stop the scheduler after three executions.
explanation: scheduleAtFixedRate targets a fixed cadence. Exceptions escaping a periodic task suppress later executions, so production tasks should handle failures deliberately.

title: Limit concurrent access with Semaphore
question: Allow at most two threads to use a resource simultaneously.
explanation: A semaphore manages permits rather than ownership of a particular monitor. Release only after a successful acquire.

title: Coordinate threads with CountDownLatch
question: Wait until three worker tasks have completed their initialization.
explanation: CountDownLatch is a one-shot gate: countDown reduces the count and await waits until it reaches zero.

title: Synchronize phases with CyclicBarrier
question: Make three workers wait until all have reached a phase boundary.
explanation: CyclicBarrier lets a fixed group rendezvous and can be reused for later phases. Cancellation or failure can break the barrier.

title: Exchange values between two threads with Exchanger
question: Exchange a value between two worker threads.
explanation: exchange() blocks until another participant arrives and swaps the supplied objects. A timed exchange can help avoid indefinite waiting.

title: Build a producer-consumer queue with BlockingQueue
question: Have one producer put messages on a queue and one consumer take them.
explanation: BlockingQueue handles coordination and backpressure. put() waits when full; take() waits when empty.

title: Implement a bounded buffer with wait and notifyAll
question: Implement a fixed-capacity integer buffer using synchronized, wait, and notifyAll.
explanation: Always test conditions in while loops because wait can wake spuriously or another thread may consume the condition first.

title: Prevent a race condition in a bank account
question: Make concurrent deposits and withdrawals safe for a shared balance.
explanation: The balance check and deduction must occur in the same critical section. Real financial code also needs validation, persistence, and transaction rules.

title: Demonstrate deadlock and avoid it with consistent lock ordering
question: Show a safe pattern for locking two resources without opposite lock ordering.
explanation: Deadlock can occur when threads acquire shared locks in opposite orders. Establish one global lock order and follow it everywhere.

title: Use tryLock to avoid waiting forever
question: Attempt to acquire a lock with a timeout and handle failure.
explanation: Timed tryLock lets a thread abandon an acquisition attempt and choose a fallback, reducing some deadlock risks.

title: Implement a thread-safe lazy singleton
question: Implement a lazy singleton using the initialization-on-demand holder idiom.
explanation: The JVM initializes Holder on first active use and guarantees class initialization synchronization, giving lazy and thread-safe initialization.

title: Implement double-checked locking correctly
question: Write a lazy singleton using double-checked locking.
explanation: volatile prevents unsafe publication/reordering from exposing a partially constructed instance. The holder idiom is often simpler.

title: Use ConcurrentHashMap for concurrent updates
question: Count word frequencies safely while multiple threads process word lists.
explanation: ConcurrentHashMap supports concurrent access. LongAdder reduces contention for heavily updated counters; wait for tasks before reading final totals.

title: Read a shared value safely with AtomicReference
question: Use AtomicReference to atomically replace a shared configuration object.
explanation: AtomicReference provides atomic reference reads and updates. Immutable configuration objects make safe publication and reasoning easier.

title: Use ThreadLocal for per-thread data
question: Give each thread its own formatter-like value using ThreadLocal.
explanation: ThreadLocal isolates values per thread. In thread pools, call remove() when the context is no longer needed to prevent stale data leaks.

title: Implement a read-write lock for shared data
question: Allow concurrent readers but exclusive writers using ReentrantReadWriteLock.
explanation: Multiple read locks can be held concurrently; the write lock is exclusive. Read-write locks are useful when reads substantially outnumber writes.

title: Use a Phaser for multiple task phases
question: Coordinate a changing set of workers across two phases with Phaser.
explanation: Phaser supports repeated synchronization phases and dynamic registration/deregistration, unlike a fixed one-shot latch.

title: Run a task asynchronously with CompletableFuture
question: Run a calculation asynchronously and transform its result.
explanation: supplyAsync returns a value asynchronously; thenApply transforms it when available. Use an explicit executor when workload isolation matters.

title: Combine two independent CompletableFuture results
question: Run two computations and combine their results.
explanation: thenCombine combines two completed results without blocking the caller until join() is invoked.

title: Handle exceptions in CompletableFuture
question: Recover from an asynchronous computation failure with a fallback value.
explanation: exceptionally maps an exceptional completion to a normal result. Handle errors deliberately so failures are not silently hidden.

title: Race tasks and use the first completion
question: Start two asynchronous tasks and use whichever completes first.
explanation: anyOf completes when any input completes, normally or exceptionally. It does not automatically cancel the losing tasks.

title: Use allOf to wait for multiple asynchronous tasks
question: Wait for several CompletableFuture tasks to finish.
explanation: allOf returns a future that completes when all supplied futures complete. It does not aggregate their values, so collect each result separately.

title: Use a custom ThreadFactory
question: Create named worker threads using a custom ThreadFactory.
explanation: A ThreadFactory centralizes thread naming and can also configure daemon status, uncaught exception handlers, or other thread properties.

title: Cancel a task using Future
question: Submit a long-running task and request cancellation.
explanation: cancel(true) requests interruption; task code must cooperate by checking interruption or handling InterruptedException. Cancellation is not forced termination.

title: Implement a timeout for a Future result
question: Wait for a task result only up to a specified duration.
explanation: Future.get(timeout, unit) bounds the caller's wait. A timeout does not automatically stop the computation; cancellation is a separate request.

title: Limit a thread pool's queued work with ThreadPoolExecutor
question: Create a pool with a bounded queue and a rejection policy.
explanation: A bounded queue provides backpressure instead of allowing unbounded task accumulation. Choose a rejection policy that fits the application.
complexity: O(queue capacity + pool size) managed tasks

title: Implement a simple parallel sum using ExecutorService
question: Split an integer array into chunks, sum each chunk concurrently, and combine the partial sums.
explanation: Independent chunks can be summed in parallel. For small arrays, thread coordination may cost more than the work saved.

title: Use ForkJoinPool for recursive parallel work
question: Sum an array using a RecursiveTask in ForkJoinPool.
explanation: ForkJoinPool uses work-stealing for divide-and-conquer tasks. A threshold avoids excessive task creation for small chunks.

title: Process a parallel stream safely
question: Compute the sum of squares using a parallel stream.
explanation: Stateless transformations and associative reductions work well with parallel streams. Avoid mutating shared state and benchmark before using parallel().

title: Find a safe way to publish an immutable object
question: Publish an immutable configuration through a volatile reference.
explanation: An immutable object avoids internal mutation races; volatile ensures readers see the latest assigned reference and the object's prior state.

title: Use a concurrent set
question: Create a set safe for concurrent additions and membership checks.
explanation: ConcurrentHashMap.newKeySet() provides a concurrent set backed by a ConcurrentHashMap.

title: Use CopyOnWriteArrayList for read-heavy workloads
question: Demonstrate a CopyOnWriteArrayList with concurrent-safe iteration.
explanation: Iterators observe a snapshot and do not throw ConcurrentModificationException. Writes copy the underlying array, so use this for read-heavy, low-write collections.

title: Use ConcurrentLinkedQueue for non-blocking producer-consumer handoff
question: Offer and poll items from a thread-safe non-blocking queue.
explanation: ConcurrentLinkedQueue is non-blocking and unbounded. Unlike BlockingQueue, poll() returns immediately when the queue is empty.

title: Use a lock condition to coordinate producer and consumer
question: Use Condition to wait for and signal availability of a value.
explanation: Condition provides wait/signal operations associated with an explicit Lock. Await must be used in a condition-checking loop.
